opening.argument: The presentation directs viewers toward a paid mining arrangement: it identifies a "one-time $99 lifetime membership" and urges them to enter a mining pool, while stating that members can "potentially mine for life." It further presents the program as producing "daily profits" and describes a binary compensation structure. The promotional opportunity extends beyond mining itself: entering a $5,000 GPU pool is linked to commissions when a participant builds a network, and a payout is tied to credits on both sides, including people signed up by sponsors. Finally, viewers are instructed to use an application that will change their IP address so they can create an account, with an alternative offer to have an account created for them. Together, these are direct enrollment, payment, return, network-commission, and access-evasion instructions.
